# Hardware and platform

The laptop's quirks decide most of raytube's design. Read this before changing
anything that touches GPUs, capture, suspend or thermals.

## Machine

MacBookPro11,5 (mid-2015 15"): Intel Core i7-4980HQ (Haswell, 4C/8T, Iris Pro
5200, i915 + i965 VA-API, `/dev/dri/renderD129`) and AMD Radeon R9 M370X
(GCN 1.0 Cape Verde, amdgpu, radeonsi, `/dev/dri/renderD128`). The internal
panel eDP-1 (2880x1800, scale 2) is driven by the **AMD** GPU (vgaswitcheroo
discrete active). Arch / Omarchy, kernel 7.2.5-3-omarchy, Hyprland 0.56.2 with
Lua config, limine UKI boot.

## AMD GPU VCE encoder crash

2026-09-23: `vah264enc` (AMD VCE 1.0) produced `ring vce0 timeout` →
`GPU Recovery Failed: -110`. Because the AMD GPU drives the panel, the screen
went black and needed a hard reboot. VCE 1.0 is also capped near 2048x1152.

**Rule:** never encode on the AMD GPU. `gst-plugin-va` was removed so nothing
auto-selects `vah264enc`. Encode on the Intel GPU with ffmpeg `h264_vaapi`
(4K24 tested at 36 fps). The AMD GPU also runs the user's speech-to-text model.

## Thermals and the guard

CPU Tjmax 100°C (coretemp "high" 84°C); GPU critical 120°C. `cast-guard.sh`
wraps every cast:

- **Quiet fan curve (default since 2026-09-26, `FAN_MODE=quiet`):** this Mac's SMC runs the
  fans flat out (6150/5700 rpm) from only ~67°C. The guard takes manual control instead:
  3500 rpm up to 70°C, rising linearly to full speed at 82°C, SMC control above that; the
  curve resumes after 60 s at ≤76°C and manual control is released on exit. At 1080p it sits
  near the 3500 rpm floor at ~69°C. (An on/off version flip-flopped every minute.)
- **Turbo off while casting (2026-09-27, `TURBO=0`):** Firefox's video work bursts the CPU from
  2.8 to 4 GHz and spiked it to 88–94°C, which throttled the CPU and knocked the fan curve off (fans
  flat out). With turbo off the cast (~5% of a core) and browser decode (Intel GPU) are unaffected;
  measured 65–73°C and 3500–3750 rpm. The fan curve uses a 10 s average; throttle/abort still act on
  every sample.

- fan boost (`FAN_MODE=auto`, and in quiet mode once the SMC has taken over): minimums
  raised to max at ≥80°C, released after 60 s at ≤70°C (`FAN_MODE=max` for always-on);
- CPU cap: `intel_pstate/max_perf_pct=60` after 3 samples ≥85°C or one spike
  ≥88°C, held ≥30 s, lifted at ≤78°C;
- abort: 2 consecutive samples ≥92°C (single turbo spikes to Tjmax are normal).

Build Rust/Go at `nice -n 19` with 2 jobs: a full-speed build during a cast
pushed the CPU to 100°C and tripped the guard.

## Hyprland screen-share leak

Hyprland 0.56.2 accumulates screen-share state. Its CPU climbs (idle 5% → 30–75%,
casting → 92%) and the cast drops to ~9 fps. A profile shows
`CScreenshareManager::outputCopyFBState` + `CScreenshareSession::isActive` at
~90%. Every capture session adds to it, including `grim` screenshots. Suspected
cause from the source: `onOutputCommit` only erases pending frames on their own
monitor's commit, so frames for a removed headless output are never erased.
**Only logging out (restarting Hyprland) clears it.** Not reported upstream yet.

## xdg-desktop-portal-hyprland freeze

xdph 1.4.1 enters a permanent "Out of buffers" → "Retrying screencopy" →
renegotiate loop when a consumer is slow or speeds up (e.g. the CPU cap
lifting). Fixed upstream in PRs #424 and #425 (merged after v1.4.1). Raytube
avoids the portal entirely; installing the patched xdph was deferred.

## Suspend and boot

- Every S3 ("deep") suspend has failed to resume: amdgpu `ring gfx test failed
  (-110)`, `amdgpu_device_ip_resume failed`, display never returns. amdgpu only
  resets the dGPU for deep sleep; **s2idle** avoids that reset (untested fix).
- Omarchy's kernel enables the Intel IOMMU, which caused boot hangs after the
  failed resume (Omarchy issue #12550). Permanent fix:
  `/etc/limine-entry-tool.d/macbook-gpu.conf` adds `intel_iommu=off noresume`,
  applied with `sudo limine-update` (UKI rebuilt).
- Ranked suspend fixes: s2idle (`/etc/systemd/sleep.conf.d/s2idle.conf`,
  `MemorySleepMode=s2idle`) → radeon driver for SI → gmux switch to Intel →
  disable lid suspend. Test with `sudo rtcwake -m freeze -s 30` with SSH
  (Tailscale <tailscale-ip>) ready.

## Firefox hardware video decode

Firefox decoded YouTube VP9 in software (~490% CPU). Fix:
`~/.config/mozilla/firefox/<profile>.default-release/user.js` (VA-API on,
VP9/AV1 MSE off so YouTube serves H.264) and
`~/.config/environment.d/60-firefox-intel-decode.conf`
(`MOZ_DRM_DEVICE=/dev/dri/renderD129`). Result: RDD 8%, Firefox total ~43%.
Apps launched from a session that predates the variable need a relaunch. The TV browser
gets the same setup from its own `user.js` (see [tv-desktop.md](tv-desktop.md#tv-browser-and-native-youtube)).

**Open question (2026-09-27):** a YouTube livestream replay was observed decoding in
**software** (`av:h264` threads, ~56% of a core) even with this setup; normal videos decode on
the Intel GPU. Cause not known yet. T-37 (enhanced-h264ify, block 60 fps) is a separate,
user-side step to halve decode work.

## Network

UFW blocks unsolicited inbound UDP. Rule added: UDP 319,320 from <apple-tv-ip>
(Apple TV PTP). Chromecast RTCP returns on the established UDP flow.
